predecessors.name: Ulus of Hülegü
predecessors.text: Sivas, Kayseri, Amasya, Tokat, Çorum, Ürgüp (Nevşehir), Canik, Şebinkarahisar, Niğde, Aksaray, Ankara and Darende: the places the page lists as incorporated, without dates

rulers.name: Ali's successor under the regent Kadi Burhan al-Din

ledger.x: 1338-1339: 'In 1338-1339, Eretna lost Darende to Qaraja' (the Dulkadir founder, who 'was continuing to enlarge his realm at the expanse of Eretna').

September-October 1343: 'After an unexpected victory at the Battle of Karanbük, against Mongol warlords competing to restore the Ilkhanate'; 'This victory resulted in the Eretnid annexation of Erzincan and several cities further east'.
ledger.cp: Mongol warlords competing to restore the Ilkhanate (Hasan Kuchak's army under Suleiman Khan)

ledger.x: 1350: 'Eretna further took advantage of the Karamanid ruler Ahmed's death in 1350, capturing Konya.'
Page silent: the page does not say when the Karamanids regained Konya; placed at Eretna's death (1352) as a bridge.
'The capital initially situated in Sivas and later Kayseri': the move is undated; placed at the accession of Muhammad I (1352), who was murdered 'in Kayseri, the capital'.
1361: 'In 1361, as a reprisal to a raid by Tatars of the Chavdar tribe', 'Ottoman ruler Murad I captured Ankara Castle from the Eretnids.'
About 1365: 'the eastern part of the realm, including Erzincan, Erzurum, and Bayburt, had come under the rule of a local figure, Ahi Ayna'.
ledger.cp: Ahi Ayna (local ruler of Erzincan, Erzurum and Bayburt)

ledger.x: Page silent on the year: 'The Karamanids invaded Niğde and Aksaray, and local Mongol tribes started disrupting the public order', placed after Muhammad's death in 1365.
1375: 'Alaeddin Bey of the Karamanids seized Kayseri, forcing Alaeddin Ali to flee to Sivas'; 'the Karamanids captured the city with the help of the Mongol tribes of Samargar and Chaykazan'.
1375: Alaeddin Ali flees from Kayseri to Sivas.
1378: 'Burhan al-Din reclaimed Kayseri and expelled Alaeddin Karamanid.'
The court returns to Kayseri with the city.
1381: 'In 1381, he took over Eretnid lands and claimed the title of sultan for himself.'

wars.name: Battle of Karanbük
wars.outcome: Eretna won on the plain of Karanbük, between Sivas and Erzincan, in September-October 1343 and annexed Erzincan and cities further east; the victory also began his independent reign (he had first used the title sultan on his coins in 1341).

wars.name: Dulkadir conquest of Darende
wars.outcome: Qaraja took Darende from Eretna in 1338-1339.

wars.name: Eretnid-Dulkadir campaign against the Mamluks at Malatya
wars.outcome: Muhammad I 'allied himself with the Dulkadirids in September 1362 in a joint campaign successfully driving the Mamluks from Malatya'; the page adds that 'this effort failed to regain Mamluk control' and does not say which of the allies kept the town.

wars.name: Karamanid invasion of Kayseri
wars.outcome: The Karamanids took Kayseri in 1375 and Burhan al-Din took it back in 1378.

certainty.note: The page lists the realm's places without dates; only Darende (1338), Erzincan (1343), Konya (1350), Ankara (1361), the east (about 1365) and Kayseri (1375, 1378) are dated.
